title: 打招呼與認識新朋友
subtitle: Greetings, polite phrases and introducing yourself

vocab.gloss: you (informal, as opposed to courteous 您)

example.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo! Nǐ shì lǎoshī ma?

vocab.gloss: to be (followed by substantives only); correct; right; true; (respectful acknowledgement of a command) very well

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyǒu.

vocab.gloss: particle indicating that a previously asked question is to be applied to the preceding word ("What about ...?", "And ...?"); particle for inquiring about location ("Where is ...?"); particle signaling a pause, to emphasize the preceding words and allow the listener time to take them on board ("ok?", "are you with me?")

example.gloss: I'm having noodles — how about you?

grammar.title: Yes/no questions with 嗎 and follow-up questions with 呢
grammar.explanation: To turn any statement into a yes/no question, just add 嗎 at the end — the word order does not change: 你好 → 你好嗎？, 你是老師 → 你是老師嗎？ To bounce a question back, or to ask the same thing about someone or something else, use just the noun or pronoun plus 呢: after 我很好，you say 你呢？(and you?). 呢 lets you skip repeating the whole question.
grammar.contrast: 嗎 vs 呢: 嗎 needs a full statement in front of it and asks for a yes/no answer. 呢 attaches to a bare noun or pronoun and reuses the question that was just asked or the topic just mentioned. If you can answer with 對 or 不, use 嗎; if you mean 'and what about X?', use 呢.
grammar.common_error: Learners pile both on at once (你好嗎呢？) or say 你嗎？ instead of 你呢？ when returning a question. Also, 嗎 is only for yes/no questions — never add it to a question that already has a question word.

passage.title: 早上好
passage.hanzi: 今天天氣很好。早上我在早餐店買了一杯奶茶，老闆說：「你好嗎？」我說：「我很好，你呢？」他說他今天很忙。我吃了早餐，搭捷運上班。在捷運上，我看見了我的好朋友小明。我說：「小明，你好！」他說他今天不上班，要去逛書店。
passage.gloss: The weather is lovely today. In the morning I bought a cup of milk tea at the breakfast shop, and the owner said, "How are you?" I said, "I'm fine, and you?" He said he was very busy today. I ate breakfast and took the MRT to work. On the MRT I saw my good friend Xiaoming. I said, "Xiaoming, hello!" He said he wasn't working today and was going to browse the bookstore.

grammar.title: 請 + verb: making a polite request
grammar.explanation: 請 goes at the FRONT of the request, before the verb. 請坐 = "please sit", 請寫你的名字 = "please write your name". You can add 你 after 請 to make it clearer who you are asking: 請你明天早一點來. Unlike English "please", 請 is never tacked on at the end of the sentence.
grammar.contrast: 請 + V ("please do it") vs. 我請你 + V ("I'll treat you / I invite you"). What decides is whether a person follows 請: 請吃飯 = "please eat"; 我請你吃飯 = "my treat, I'm buying you a meal."
grammar.common_error: Learners copy English word order and say things like "坐請" or put 請 at the end of the sentence. 請 must come first. Also, 請 is not needed with 謝謝 — and when someone says 對不起, the reply is 沒關係, not 不客氣 (不客氣 answers 謝謝).

examples.hanzi: 請坐一下,老闆現在很忙。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zuò yíxià, lǎobǎn xiànzài hěn máng.
examples.gloss: Please have a seat, the boss is busy right now.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ míngtiān zǎo yìdiǎn lái.
examples.gloss: Please come a bit earlier tomorrow.

grammar.title: 謝謝 / 不客氣 / 對不起 / 沒關係 as reply pairs
grammar.pattern: 謝謝 → 不客氣;對不起 → 沒關係
grammar.explanation: These four words come in two fixed pairs in daily Taiwan life. When someone thanks you (謝謝), you answer 不客氣. When someone apologises (對不起), you answer 沒關係. 再見 closes the conversation.
grammar.contrast: 不客氣 vs. 沒關係: 不客氣 = "you're welcome" (after thanks); 沒關係 = "it's OK, no harm done" (after an apology). The trigger word decides which one you use.
grammar.common_error: Saying 不客氣 after someone apologises. If you hear 對不起, say 沒關係.

examples.gloss: Thanks for the tea. — You're welcome!

examples.hanzi: 對不起,我的腳踏車太快了。沒關係。
examples.pinyin: Duìbùqǐ, wǒ de jiǎotàchē tài kuài le. Méiguānxì.
examples.gloss: Sorry, my bike was going too fast. — It's fine.

examples.hanzi: 時間晚了,我要走了,再見!
examples.pinyin: Shíjiān wǎn le, wǒ yào zǒu le, zàijiàn!
examples.gloss: It's late, I have to go. Bye!

passage.title: 雨天的傘
passage.hanzi: 今天早上下大雨,我沒帶傘,在捷運站外面很冷。一個同學走近我,說:「這是我的傘,請你用。」我說:「謝謝你!」他說:「不客氣。」我們一起走路去學校。我走得太快,他的書有一點水,我說對不起,他說沒關係。學校近了,我們說再見。
passage.gloss: It rained hard this morning and I didn't have an umbrella; it was cold outside the MRT station. A classmate came up to me and said, "This is my umbrella, please use it." I said, "Thank you!" He said, "You're welcome." We walked to school together. I walked too fast and his book got a little wet; I said sorry, and he said it didn't matter. When school was close, we said goodbye.

grammar.title: Question words 什麼 / 誰 stay where the answer goes
grammar.pattern: 主語 + 叫／是／要 + 什麼（名字）／誰？
grammar.explanation: In Mandarin you do not move the question word to the front. Put 什麼 or 誰 exactly in the slot where the answer would appear: 我叫小文 → 你叫什麼？ 他是小文 → 他是誰？ 什麼 asks about a thing or a name, 誰 asks about a person. Sentences with a question word are already questions, so the word order is the same as a statement.
grammar.contrast: Compare with 嗎 questions: 「你叫小文嗎？」is a yes/no question about a name you already guessed; 「你叫什麼名字？」asks for the name itself. You choose 嗎 when you have a guess to confirm, and 什麼/誰 when you have no information. The two never combine.
grammar.common_error: Learners copy English word order and say 什麼你叫？ instead of 你叫什麼？, or they tack 嗎 onto the end (你叫什麼名字嗎？). Never add 嗎 to a sentence that already has 什麼 or 誰.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì shéi? Wǒ bú rènshì tā.

passage.title: 新同學
passage.hanzi: 今天早上，我在學校認識了一個新同學。他叫小文，家在台中。他不太愛說話，可是對我很好。中午我們一起吃便當，我買了一杯珍珠奶茶請他。晚上他打電話給我，我說：「喂，你是誰？」他說：「是我啦！」我們說了半個小時的話。認識新朋友很好。
passage.gloss: This morning I met a new classmate at school. He's called Xiaowen, and his home is in Taichung. He doesn't much like to talk, but he's very nice to me. At noon we ate lunch boxes together, and I bought a cup of bubble milk tea for him. In the evening he called me. I said, "Hello, who is this?" He said, "It's me!" We talked for half an hour. Meeting new friends is great.
